scope: Stage 4c of the 1st development plan: mode-resolved LSWT structure factor (one-magnon transverse and exact Bragg), broadened spectra, and bond correlations, reusing the stored diagonalization (D26).

added.code-space/spintoolkit/observables/struc: structure_factor, StructureFactor (energies, weights W^{ab}, elastic, bragg, zero_mode; static, trace, neutron, spectrum), bond_correlations

LSWTResult gains positions and local_frames; eigenvalue docstring corrected (hole-branch energies are positive)

conventions: S^a(q) = N^{-1/2} sum_r exp(-i q.r) S^a_r (full positions, per site); delta S_i = sqrt(S_i/2)[(x_i - i y_i) a_i + (x_i + i y_i) a_i^dagger] in the Hamiltonian's local frame; particle modes at +w with 1 + n_B, hole components at -w with n_B; Bragg I(G) = F F^dagger / N_s^2 with F = sum_i m_i exp(-i G.tau_i), m_i = (S_i - <n_i>) n_i; the longitudinal two-magnon continuum (O(S^0)) is excluded.

legacy_correlations.diagnosis: legacy static S(q) = N_s x (per-site S(q) computed with an extra exp(-i q.tau_i) on top of the full-position-gauge H(k)): per-cell normalization and a doubled sublattice phase; get_quantum_spin_corr_mat also repeats the [mu+Ns, nu] element instead of [mu+Ns, nu+Ns] for sublattice-resolved output

findings: The existing observables/correlations.py (untested, unwired) disagrees with ED-validated weights: its static S(q) equals N_s times a structure factor with an extra sublattice phase applied on top of the full-position-gauge H(k); sublattice-resolved output also repeats one matrix element. It is left unchanged and not used; keeping or removing it is a user decision.
Bragg vectors of an ordered state coincide with Goldstone zero modes; the structure factor reports NaN inelastic weights there (zero_mode flag) and still returns the elastic part.
decisions: D26 (2026-09-30): one-magnon transverse plus exact elastic Bragg (two-magnon longitudinal continuum later); mode-resolved weights as the primary output with a broadening helper; new implementation, the existing Correlations only as a comparison; bond correlations included (energy cross-check), general real-space correlations later.
